meta.gift: order, season, and the slow sap that binds moments in sequence
meta.waning: the Root greys and splits; hours repeat, orchards fruit with last year's fruit
meta.curse_desc: growth rings surface on the flesh of the afflicted, one for each hour they relive
veils: The pruning-hooks of the church are not symbols; something is still cut from the Root each season, and burned unseen.
The Root grew from a buried corpse, and the order it grants is that corpse's refusal to be forgotten.
The corpse is not dead but dreaming in sequence; the seasons are its heartbeats, and the rot began when it started to wake.
meta.epigraph: Of the Pale Root little now is spoken, and less is true. Gather what the old things still remember, and be sparing with belief.

ages.name: the Age of the Gift
ages.blurb: the Pale Root gave the world order, season, and the slow sap that binds moments in sequence.

ages.name: the Age of Names
ages.blurb: The gods withdrew to their high seats and mortals learned to matter. Then the waning began: the Root greys and splits; hours repeat, orchards fruit with last year's fruit.

ages.name: the Age of Dusk
ages.blurb: The present age. The gods are silent, the roads belong to the marked, and pilgrims walk toward rumours of a cure.

e1.text: the Pale Root rose (or was raised — the tellings differ) and gave the world order, season, and the slow sap that binds moments in sequence.

e2.text: Ghalenmund, god of secrets, locks, and the spaces between, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e3.text: Thaliagrim, god of war and the keeping of thresholds, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e4.text: Queliamund, god of graves and the ledger of names, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e6.text: The Sap of Ghalenmund was wrought as regalia of Ghalenmund's throne.

e8.text: The Ring of Thaliagrim was wrought as regalia of Thaliagrim's throne.

e10.text: The Graft of Queliamund was wrought as regalia of Queliamund's throne.

e11.text: Iriorn, the Ungrown, rose against the thrones. Ghalenmund led the gods to war.
e11.hidden: Thaliagrim treated with Iriorn in secret and was spared what followed.

e12.text: Iriorn was defeated and sealed beneath Iraeienvault; the seal was bought with the lives of 5 champions.

e13.text: The waning began: the Root greys and splits; hours repeat, orchards fruit with last year's fruit. Mortals called the affliction the Ringing-rot: growth rings surface on the flesh of the afflicted, one for each hour they relive.

e14.text: Draessrion the Grey founded the Order of the Graft at Ulirwyncradle, sworn to stand against the Ringing-rot.

e15.text: The Church of Queliamund was raised at Karaeosvault; Lowyn the Twice-crowned took its first pulpit, preaching that the waning is a trial and the faithful will be spared.

e16.text: Belwyn the Unbowed was cast out of Church of Queliamund and founded the Cult of the Patient Below, teaching that the gods themselves caused the waning.
e16.hidden: The heresy is nearer the truth than the sermon.

e17.text: Ostorthas the Grey united the river-clans and was crowned in Galomerebarrow; the realm took the name Olagarcradle.

e18.text: At the urging of Belwyn, the saint Caliadis of the Long Vigil was given to the Pale Root in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.
e18.hidden: The rite did not restore anything. It only fed the waning more slowly — and Belwyn suspected as much.

e19.text: Wrensila the Quiet, sword-hand of Ostorthas, opened the gates of Galomerebarrow to the Order of the Graft over a grievance no chronicle agrees on.
e19.hidden: Wrensila acted on a promise from the Cult of the Patient Below: that the marked of their house would be spared the Ringing-rot. The promise was not kept.

e20.text: Olagarcradle fell. Ostorthas the Grey died at the foot of their own throne; the crown was carried away and never worn again.

e21.text: Wrensila was found at Kaemisvault bearing the Ringing-rot, and was not spared.

e22.text: Ghalenmund, god of secrets, locks, and the spaces between, descended below the world to look upon the Pale Root directly, and did not return.
e22.hidden: Ghalenmund found the truth of the waning, and chose to stay.

e23.text: Eloric the Unmarked, last-sworn of the Order of the Graft, set out for the place where Ghalenmund was lost, carrying the order's final blessing.

e24.text: Eloric was last seen at the edge of the deep roads. The order keeps a vigil that has not ended.

e25.text: Pilgrims of the Cult of the Patient Below were found digging at the seal of Iriorn. The wardens hanged nine; the digging continued.
e25.hidden: The seal has been failing on its own since the waning began. The cult only follows the cracks.
